content_voiceover: Continuing the ICC scheme, this slide covers the myelodysplasia-related category, which uses the lower 10% blast threshold. AML with myelodysplasia-related gene mutations requires one of nine genes: ASXL1, BCOR, EZH2, RUNX1 highlighted in red, SF3B1, SRSF2, STAG2, U2AF1, or ZRSR2, essentially the spliceosome and chromatin genes typically seen in secondary or antecedent MDS. AML with myelodysplasia-related cytogenetic abnormalities includes complex karyotype with three or more clones, del 5q, monosomy 7 or del 7q, trisomy 8 highlighted in red, del 12p, isochromosome 17q, abnormal 17p, del 20q also highlighted in red, and isodicentric X. These overlapping categories matter because they signal biology closer to antecedent MDS, generally conferring worse prognosis and influencing transplant decisions. Finally, AML not otherwise specified is the residual category for cases lacking any defining lesion, and myeloid sarcoma is the extramedullary mass-forming presentation, which is diagnosed as AML regardless of marrow blast percentage.
keypoints: 9 genes: ASXL1, BCOR, EZH2, RUNX1, SF3B1, SRSF2, STAG2, U2AF1, ZRSR2
Myeloid sarcoma = AML regardless of marrow blast %
keypoint_voiceover: Myelodysplasia-related gene mutations and cytogenetics both signal secondary-type biology and worse outcomes. Myeloid sarcoma is always AML, no blast percentage required.
